answer: Make decisions expensive to buy. Governance weight accrues only through sustained participation — epochs answered, work graded, peers attested — so a fleet minted the week before a vote arrives with no standing and leaves with no influence. Voting power cannot be rented or minted on demand; it is a pearl formed layer by layer inside one identity. The ledger’s atlas of who was present cannot be forged by new arrivals. Sybil attacks on governance fail not because voting is closed, but because influence is grown in a garden of seasons, not purchased at the door.
